title: Checkboxes, radio buttons, and select lists in PHP forms
answer: An unchecked checkbox sends nothing at all, so always read it with ??. Name a group of checkboxes with [] to receive them as an array. A select list sends the value of the chosen option, not its label.
pitfall: Reading $_POST['agree'] directly when the box is unchecked raises an undefined index warning. Use isset or ?? for every optional field.

title: Post/Redirect/Get - stop double form submission on refresh
answer: After a successful POST, redirect to a result page instead of printing the result directly. When the user refreshes, the browser repeats a harmless GET instead of resubmitting the payment or order. Store a one-time flash message in the session to show after the redirect. This example is syntax-checked only because it sends HTTP headers.
pitfall: Code after header('Location: ...') keeps running unless you call exit. Always exit immediately after a redirect.

title: GET and POST forms - reading form data safely
answer: Use GET for searches and shareable links, and POST for actions that change data. Read submitted values from $_POST with ?? defaults, trim them, and check they exist before use. This example is syntax-checked only because it needs a real form submission.
pitfall: Accepting a state-changing action over GET means a link or image can trigger it. Actions like delete, pay, and publish must use POST plus a CSRF token.

title: Validation and sanitization - filter_var, required checks, error messages
answer: Validation rejects bad data, sanitization cleans it. Check required fields first, then validate formats with filter_var for email and URLs, and range checks for numbers. Collect all errors and show them together instead of stopping at the first one.
output: A valid email is required. Age must be 13 or more.
pitfall: Sanitizing is not validating. Stripping characters from an invalid email and accepting it still stores a broken address. Reject invalid input instead of silently fixing it.
